summary: Mechanically the design is sound and I found no geometry blocker. Brief features are all present and sized right (pan +/-90, tilt -35..+65, captive 1/4-20 nut, CM3 on 4 x M2). The load path is two-sided, FEA hot spots sit at the tab pilots and window corners, sweeps are clear, and mass is 59 g against a 90 g limit. It fails on one major finding: docs/ENGINEERING.md 10b requires an electrical system (power, signal, wiring, run declared) for every project that moves anything. pan_tilt has none, so the owner is not told how to power and wire two servos through a +/-90 deg pan. Everything else is minor.

findings.issue: No `electrical:` / `wiring:` block (kerf warns). ENGINEERING.md 10b says every project that moves or powers anything must derive the whole electrical system: servo supply/BEC as a catalog item, power_budget, run_time, and each run declared in `wiring:` with gauge and cut length >= routed length + 15 %. DESIGN.md A6 only gives 5 V >= 1 A and 470-1000 uF in prose, and the review history says 'not done'. Nothing proves the supply can feed two SG90s (stall about 0.65 A each), and nothing defines the servo-lead and FPC runs that must survive pan +/-90 deg and tilt -35..+65. The tilt servo lead is only tied to the yoke ledge and then hangs free past the pan axis, where it will wind around the horn at +/-90.
findings.fix: Add an `electrical:` block with a catalog-sourced 5 V supply or BEC and a controller or PCA9685 (catalog entries exist), a power_budget at the 2 x stall peak and a run_time. Add `wiring:` for the two servo leads (Pololu 300 mm servo lead is in the catalog), with cut lengths from the worst pose and the >= 60 mm slack loop at the pan axis. Mention the 470-1000 uF capacitor in the BOM. Re-run kerf check.

findings.issue: Pan-horn screws are M2 x 8 through the 6 mm plate, which leaves only 2.0 mm of thread in a horn disc whose thickness (2.0) and bolt circle (12) are catalog ESTIMATES (confidence: estimate; no vendor drawing). The tilt horn screws (M2 x 6 through the 3.5 mm arm) rely on the same estimate.
findings.fix: Measure the purchased horns before printing. If the disc is thinner than 2 mm, shorten yoke_t or use a shim, and update the catalog value.

findings.issue: The lead slot is 3.9 mm wide (y 2.2..6.1) and offset about 2 mm from the centre line where the SG90 lead leaves the case, leaving a 1.3 mm wall to the tab pilot. The 3-pin connector housing only passes edge-on. The slot floor sits at servo_floor_z (10 mm), about at the lead exit height. The printed M2 pilots are good for only a few cycles.
findings.fix: Print the base first and test-fit the servo lead. Widen the slot to about 6 mm or centre it if it is tight. Use M2 heat-set inserts if the servo is removed often.

findings.issue: The tilt-servo window has a 12.8 mm top bridge, ledge slots and the FPC notch. The part sheet shows ragged window edges at the top of the +Y wall, and the seat of the servo case depends on bridge quality. Only 1.9 % overhang is reported.
findings.fix: Check the sliced preview of the bridge. Ream the window after printing if it sags.

findings.issue: 3.5 % of the surface needs support (teardrop and 45 deg holes). The 2.4 mm hex-key access teardrops and the knuckle floor hole may close up or string, which would stop a 1.5 mm key getting through.
findings.fix: Say in ASSEMBLY.md to ream the 2.4 mm holes with a 2.5 mm drill.

findings.issue: The tripod screw protrusion window of 5.5-8 mm (A2) is an assumption, because the pan servo sits only 2 mm above an 8 mm tip. The 40 x 26 mm footprint is small for a head that sits 13 mm off-centre on a roughly 70 mm tall stack.
findings.fix: Keep the warning in ASSEMBLY.md and consider a wider base or skirt for soft surfaces.

findings.issue: The cam_clear margin (bracket to yoke) is 0.9 mm against a 0.8 mm limit, which equals the 0.9 mm pivot gap. FDM tolerance on both parts can consume that margin, and the M3 screw head is told to be backed off only 1/8 turn.
findings.fix: Check the pivot rotation freely after assembly. Use a shoulder screw, or increase pivot_gap to 1.0 (the param max) if it binds.
